extracted.intended_audience: authors of manuscripts accepted by Acta Mathematica
extracted.subtask_description: Instructions for preparing and submitting final (accepted) manuscripts to the journal Acta Mathematica, including formatting, reference style, figure policies, file naming, and electronic submission procedure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consult recent issue for style and layout
rubrics_metrics.description: Please consult a recent issue of the Acta Mathematica to get a general idea for the style and the layout.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should use a recent published issue as the model for typography, formatting, and layout conventions. This is the primary guide for manuscript appearance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editor approval for non-typographical changes
rubrics_metrics.description: Note that changes other than typographical must be approved by the editor in charge.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After acceptance, only typographical changes are assumed allowable without further permission; any substantive or non-typographic alterations require explicit approval from the handling editor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference list completeness and relevance
rubrics_metrics.description: We are quite careful with the reference lists. We therefore ask you to fill in any missing data in the reference list, update the references as much as possible, and delte any reference that is not relevant to the current version of your paper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Before submission ensure every reference has full bibliographic data (authors, title, journal/book, volume, year, pages, publisher info as appropriate) and remove irrelevant or obsolete citations. (Original text contains 'delte' = delete.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Colour figures printing policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Acta Mathematica is printed in black/white. If you wish to have figures printed in colour, you have to be prepared to contribute to the extra costs. In the online version colour figures will appear free of charge.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should assume print will be grayscale; request for color printing in the printed journal may incur extra charges to be borne by the author. Colour in the online edition is provided without charge.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abstract required for web posting
rubrics_metrics.description: Please add at the beginning of your paper an abstract that will not be printed, but put on the web.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Every accepted paper must include an abstract placed at the start of the manuscript; the abstract is intended for web presentation (all Acta Mathematica papers are presented with abstract and reference list on the web at springer.com/11511). The abstract will not appear in the printed journal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use Math Reviews / Zentralblatt to complete references
rubrics_metrics.description: Before electronically submitting a paper accepted by the Acta Mathematica, authors should ensure that the reference list is complete. Mathematical Reviews and Zentralblatt für Mathematik contain the necessary information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors are advised to consult MR and Zbl to obtain missing bibliographic details and ensure standard, complete citations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Journal reference format
rubrics_metrics.description: References should have the following format: Journals — Anderson, J. M., Clunie, J. and Pommerenke, C., On Bloch functions and normal functions. J. Reine Angew. Math., 270 (1974), 12-37.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Format: Author(s) (surname, initials), Title. Journal_abbreviation, volume (year), page-range. Use the journal's conventional abbreviations and include volume, year and pages as shown in the example.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-Latin-alphabet paper reference format
rubrics_metrics.description: Papers not originally written in the Latin alphabet — Naboko, S. N., On the dense point spectrum of Schrödinger and Dirac operators. Teoret. Mat. Fiz., 68 (1986), 18-28 (Russian); English translation in Theoret. and Math. Phys., 68 (1986), 646-653.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For works originally in other alphabets/languages include original bibliographic entry (journal, volume, pages, language) and, where applicable, provide the English translation citation after a semicolon as in the example.

rubrics_metrics.name: Book reference format
rubrics_metrics.description: Books — Akhiezer, N. I., The Classical Moment Problem and Some Related Questions in Analysis. Hafner, New York, 1965.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Format: Author(s), Title. Publisher, Place, Year. Include series information if appropriate (example: Cambridge Tracts in Math., 95).

rubrics_metrics.name: Conference proceedings reference format
rubrics_metrics.description: Conference proceedings, etc — Kohn, J. J., Methods of partial differential equations in complex analysis, in Several Complex Variables (Williamstown, MA, 1975), pp. 215-237. Proc. Symp. Pure Math., 30. Amer. Math. Soc., Providence, RI, 1977.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Format: Author, Title of contribution, in Book/Proceedings Title (location, year), page-range. Series title and number, publisher, place, year. Include both contribution pages and series/proceedings details as shown.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preprint / accepted-but-unprinted citation format
rubrics_metrics.description: Preprints and papers accepted but not yet printed — Cegrell, U., The general definition of the complex Monge-Ampère operator. Preprint, 2000. Andrievskii, V. V., On the Green function for the complement of a finite number of real intervals. To appear in Const. Approx.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For preprints indicate 'Preprint, YEAR'. For accepted but not printed papers use 'To appear in [Journal/Proceedings]'. Provide as much bibliographic detail as available.

rubrics_metrics.name: TeX filename convention
rubrics_metrics.description: The name of the TeX file should be the surname of the (first) author with the extension .tex. If the surname has more than eight letters, use only the first eight.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submit the main .tex file named exactly as specified (surname.tex), truncating surnames longer than eight characters to the first eight letters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include macros and style files
rubrics_metrics.description: Any macros or style files should be included.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide all custom .sty, .cls, and macro files used to compile the manuscript so the editors can reproduce the source. Do not omit auxiliary files.

rubrics_metrics.name: Figure file format: encapsulated PostScript (.eps)
rubrics_metrics.description: Figures should be submitted separately as encapsulated postscript (.eps) files.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submit each figure as a separate .eps file (vector/encapsulated PostScript) rather than embedding raster images in the .tex source. Follow common EPS conventions for sizing and fonts.

rubrics_metrics.name: File submission method and include PDF of final version
rubrics_metrics.description: Electronic files including a pfd file of the final version should be submitted as attachments to an e-mail message to Margareta Wiberg, address see below.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Attach all source files and a final-version PDF of the manuscript to an email addressed to the journal contact (Margareta Wiberg). Note: the page contains a typographical error 'pfd' — intended meaning is 'pdf'. Include contact details as provided for submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contact for further questions
rubrics_metrics.description: Further questions should be addressed to Margareta Wiberg via e-mail or by regular mail to Acta Mathematica, Institut Mittag-Leffler, Auravägen 17, SE-182 60 Djursholm, SWEDEN.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the provided email or postal address for queries about final submission, file formats, or editorial issues; the handling editor/contact person is Margareta Wiberg.
